extraFacts.fact: Wave 4 products are API certified and supplied with the API monogram by API-licensed manufacturers to the applicable specification: API 6A, API 16A, API 16C, API 16D or API 7K.

Hammer unions of different figure numbers must never be joined: the male half of a 602 or 1002 union can make up into a 1502 wing nut and look made up, then separate under pressure. Mismatched unions have caused fatalities and IADC recommends colour coding, go/no-go gauges and segregated storage.
NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 sets material requirements for equipment used in H2S-containing oil and gas production.
ANSI raised-face flanged valve ends are dimensioned to ASME B16.5.
extraFacts.source: ASME B16.5 Pipe Flanges and Flanged Fittings

faqs.q: What is a 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve used for?
faqs.a: A 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve (15K, sour service) is a spring-loaded relief valve that lifts at its set pressure to protect the line or vessel from over-pressure. NACE MR0175 compliant — sour-well frac iron over-pressure protection.

faqs.q: What does the Weco 1502 union end on the 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve mean?
faqs.a: On this spring-loaded pressure relief valve the listing gives a 2 in 1502 male Weco union on the inlet and a female union on the outlet. 1502 is the union figure number, which fixes the thread, seal and pressure class of the joint, so mate this spring-loaded pressure relief valve only with a union of the same figure number and thread.

faqs.q: What end connections does the 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve have?
faqs.a: On the 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve (sour service) the inlet is 2 in 1502 Male Weco Union and the outlet is 2 in 1502 Female Weco Union. A union end makes up quickly in flow iron; never join two different figure numbers.

faqs.q: Should I choose the 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve or the 3-1/8 in 5,000 psi version?
faqs.a: Choose by line size, pressure and service. This listing is 2 in at 15,000 psi (sour service); the [3-1/8 in 5,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve](/p/pressure-relief-valve-spring-loaded-3-1-8-in-5m-flanged-5-000-psi-sour-service) is rated 5,000 psi with 3-1/8 in API 6A 5M Flanged (RTJ) on the inlet. Match pressure class and end connection of the mating iron.

faqs.q: What is the working pressure of the 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve, and how is it tested?
faqs.a: The 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve with its Forged AISI 4130 body is rated 15,000 psi working pressure (15K class). The pressure on the listing is the body rating; the set pressure is made to order and is a separate figure you specify on the RFQ. Match every component in the line to this rating.

faqs.q: What materials is the 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve made from?
faqs.a: The 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve has a Forged AISI 4130 body; the trim is 316SS disc + nozzle, NACE-compliant Inconel X-750 spring and the seals are PEEK back-up + HNBR primary seals. Body, trim and seals are listed to NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 with material class EE. The spring is hardness-controlled to suit the service.

faqs.q: Is the 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve suitable for sour (H2S) service, and which standard does it meet?

faqs.q: What set pressure can I specify for the 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded relief valve?
faqs.a: The listing figure of 15,000 psi is the body rating, not the set pressure. The set pressure is made to order, so state it on the RFQ together with the media, flow rate and temperature, and read the [oilfield pressure relief valve guide](/blog/oilfield-pressure-relief-valves) before choosing.

faqs.q: How is the 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve operated and maintained?
faqs.a: On the 2 in 15,000 psi spring-loaded pressure relief valve, the spring sets the lift pressure and it is factory-set to the pressure ordered, so do not adjust it in the field. Inspect and test-lift the valve at the interval set by your plant procedure, and replace the seals after any lift. See the [oilfield pressure relief valve guide](/blog/oilfield-pressure-relief-valves).
